a:r.a:t: Oxidation of Multiple Carbohydrates Involves Glycolysis

p:cNvPr.descr: An illustration of the entry of dietary glycogen, starch, disaccharides, and hexoses into the preparatory stage of glycolysis. It begins at the top left with trehalose in a pink box. It has an arrow pointing down and right to D-glucose. To the right of the arrow is trehalase in blue. D-glucose is a hexagon with thick lines at the three bottom lines. At the left point, H bonds down to HO. At the top left point, CH2OH bonds down to H (inside hexagon). The top right point is O. At the right point, H bonds down to OH. At the bottom right point, H (inside hexagon) bonds down to OH, and the bottom left point has OH (inside hexagon) bonding down to H. This is all in a pink box. To the left is sucrose in a pink box. Below this is an arrow that points down and right to D-glucose. To the right is sucrose in blue. The arrow also points down and right to D-fructose in a pink box. D-fructose is a pentagon with thick lines on the three bottom sides. At the left point, HOCH2 bonds down to H. The top point is O. At the right point, CH2OH bonds down to OH. At the bottom right point, HO (inside pentagon) bonds down to H, and at the bottom left point, H bonds down to OH. Below this is an arrow pointing down. To the left of the arrow is ATP, and to the right is fructokinase in blue. Below this is fructose 1-phosphate. Below this is an arrow that splits left and right. To the right of the arrow is fructose-1 phosphate aldolase in blue. The left arrow points to glyceraldehyde. The right arrow points to dihydroxyacetone phosphate. There is a plus sign between the two. Both glyceraldehyde and dihydroxyacetone phosphate have arrows pointing down then right to glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate. To the left of the arrow from glyceraldehyde is ATP. To the right is triose kinase in blue. To the right of the arrow pointing from dihydroxyacetone phosphate is triose phosphate isomerase in blue. To the right and at the top, lactose is in a pink box and points down to D-glucose. This also has another arrow pointing right to D-galactose. This is the same as D-glucose, but at the left point, HO bonds down to H. To the right of the D-glucose box is another pink box with dietary glycogen; starch. This has an an arrow on the left, pointing left, to D-glucose. H2O merges into this arrow. Below the arrow is alpha-amylase in blue. To the right of this box is endogenous glycogen in a pink box. It has an arrow pointing down and left to glucose 1-phosphate in the middle. Pi joins this arrow, and to the right is phosphorylase in blue. Two successive arrows point down and left from D-galactose to UDP-glucose, which points left to glucose 1-phosphate. From glucose 1-phosphate is an arrow pointing down to glucose 6-phosphate. To the right of the arrow is phosphoglucomutase in blue. An arrow from D-glucose points down and right to glucose 6-phosphate. To the left of this arrow is hexokinase in blue. To the right is ATP. Glucose 6-phosphate has an arrow below pointing down to fructose 6-phosphate. To the right is a pink box with D-Mannose. This is the same as D-glucose, but at the bottom right HO (inside the hexagon) bonds down to H. From this box is an arrow pointing down and left to mannose 6-phosphate. To the left of this arrow is ATP. To the right is hexokinase in blue. Mannose 6-phosphate has an arrow pointing to fructose 6-phosphate. Below this arrow is phosphomannose isomerase in blue. Below fructose 6-phosphate is an arrow pointing down to fructose 1,6-bisphosphate. Below this is an arrow pointing down to glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate.
